why_trail.why: Rework 3 is a prose-only repair of two claim families that three passes missed because every grep keyed on the deleted symbol name. The derive family must say the engine derives nothing anywhere (ADMIRAL_RULING-2 N2, shipped at 84d949eb); the ownership family must carry ADMIRAL_RULING-1 R1's narrowing — the lease guards only where a lease exists, the leaseless widening is accepted, forgeable is not absent, and an active foreign lease is unchanged. Three stale passages are named (two in checklist_engine.main()'s load-time comment block, one in spine_lifecycle.build_origin's docstring); the gate turns on whether my sweep finds anything the reviewer's did not.

The claim-level sweep is claim-shaped, not symbol-shaped, and matches across wrapped comment/docstring lines -- which is what hid B1, whose stale sentence breaks after 'derived'. 1589 hits over 10224 tracked files: 64 live, 1525 in the record zone (.agent-work/, episodes/, map/) which is counted and never repaired. Of the 64: 6 hit-lines are the 4 stale claims in 2 files (exactly the three passages the reviewer named -- no fourth), 4 are true claims whose consumer count needs harmonizing, 6 already correct, 19 fenced to g3/lane A, 29 unrelated. classify_hits.py refuses on any unclassified live hit, so 64/64 is mechanical.

Four stale claims repaired in two files: main()'s derive sentence and ownership sentence, and build_origin's parenthesis which held one of each. Both repaired ownership passages carry R1 in full -- leaseless only, never claimed or released, WIDENED and accepted, forgeable is not absent, active foreign lease unchanged -- stated, not hedged. The consumer count is now one identical sentence in all four copies that state it: two real consumers (the shape question g2 deleted, #315's cwd thread R3 re-homed) plus a third R2 withdrew before it existed. check_claims_repaired.py extracts six segments by their own anchors so a clause in the header cannot cover for main(), and it runs the same clause set against 84d949eb's blobs: 29 problems there, 0 on the tree.

The pipeline prints 12 lines, every one of them the build_origin docstring -- expected, since a docstring line is not a # line. The stronger property behind it: for both changed files under scripts/, the module AST with every docstring blanked is byte-identical between 84d949eb and the working tree, so no statement, argument or constant moved. Comments never enter an AST, so that comparison isolates exactly the executable content.

A prose-only change must not move the suite. Baseline at 84d949eb is 3170 passed / 5 skipped / 0 failed; the check clears __pycache__ first (a cache built in another tree fails test_bytecode_cache_provenance by name) and scrubs SPINE_* and CREW_SCRATCH_DIR, without which lane E's fenced test_crew_launcher case fails on ambient contamination inside a crew session. The map was rebuilt first and left map/ clean, so the freshness test cannot fire.

A docstring edit can move entity text in the map, so the map is rebuilt rather than assumed fresh. It rebuilds clean: git status --porcelain -- map/ is empty, so this rework moved no map entity -- consistent with a change that touched only comment and docstring prose.

Counted against 84d949eb's blobs with comment markers stripped first -- without that the engine header's own citation is invisible, because it wraps after '2026-08-15'. Six supersession occurrences at base, six on the tree, file for file; the 2026-08-16 worktree-is-location citation is still exactly one, in the table docstring, which is why that sentence was left untouched.

The result carries the three load-bearing pieces the handoff names -- C1's sweep with its commands and counts, C3's two passages quoted side by side (generated from the files, not retyped), and C5's verbatim output with the reason it is non-empty (a docstring line is not a # line) -- plus the confirmatory C6/C7/C8, three triage candidates and the workflow feedback.
